title: When a simpler tool is better

sections.skill: Choose a simpler tool when it fits better

questions.prompt: Which tool is best for adding up 40 expenses exactly?

choices.text: A generative chatbot asked to add the numbers in a single long paragraph

questions.intro: A generative AI tool is not always the best tool. A CALCULATOR or SPREADSHEET is better for arithmetic and totals, because it computes exactly every time. A SEARCH ENGINE or OFFICIAL WEBSITE is better for current facts like hours, prices and rules, because it points to the source. A DICTIONARY or THESAURUS is quick for word meanings. A CALENDAR with reminders is better for deadlines. Generative tools shine at drafting, rephrasing, brainstorming and explaining. Choosing the simpler tool when it fits saves time and avoids errors.

sections.title: Apply it

sections.skill: Combine tools and spot disguised tasks

questions.prompt: An email to a landlord includes a total of past payments. What is the best workflow?

choices.text: Draft with AI; compute the total in a spreadsheet
Let the AI tool compute the total inside the email

questions.correct_answer: Draft with AI; compute the total in a spreadsheet
questions.intro: Sometimes the best answer is a combination: draft an email with a generative tool, but compute the figures in it with a spreadsheet and copy dates from the official calendar. Watch for tasks that look like writing but are really lookups ("What is the return deadline?") or calculations ("How much do I owe?"). Also consider cost and privacy: a simple offline tool may avoid sharing information at all. Ask: what does this task really need, exact math, a current source, or new wording?
